sections.heading: The road to 15 August — and its price

blocks.text: The endgame ran: 1945-46 elections (League swept Muslim seats — the mandate it lacked in 1937) → **Cabinet Mission's** failed unity design → **Direct Action (16 Aug 1946)** and the riot chain (Calcutta → **Noakhali (Oct) → Bihar → Garhmukteshwar → Rawalpindi (Mar 1947)**) → Interim Government's dysfunction (League's obstruction from within) → Attlee's **20 February 1947** deadline statement (transfer by June 1948; Mountbatten sent) → **Mountbatten's 3 June Plan** (partition + dominion status + princely choice) — accepted by Congress as 'the freezing of a civil war' — → **Indian Independence Act (18 July 1947)** → **Radcliffe awards published 17 August** — two days *after* freedom: boundaries revealed to already-moving millions.

rows: Human cost
Deaths ~**5-10+ lakh** (estimates range to 20); **~1.4-1.8 crore displaced** — history's largest forced migration; ~1 lakh women abducted/violated (Recovery Act 1949's painful sequel)
Why Congress accepted

Exhaustion + ungovernability of coalition (Interim Govt) + riots' momentum + fear of balkanisation beyond two states + Patel's 'diseased limb' realism + Mountbatten's speed; Gandhi's dissent stood apart — he spent 15 August fasting in Calcutta
Institutional surgery
Armies, assets (₹55 crore dispute → Gandhi's last fast), records, even instruments divided; **Punjab & Bengal partitioned by Radcliffe**; Sylhet & NWFP referendums
**Rehabilitation**

Ministry of Relief & Rehabilitation; camps (Kurukshetra's ~3 lakh); **Nilokheri (S.K. Dey's township-with-work model)**, Faridabad; evacuee-property law; East-Punjab land allotment (graded cuts — Tarlok Singh's 'standard acre'); Bengal's slower tragedy (continuing influx → Dandakaranya scheme later); refugees rebuilt Delhi, Kolkata — displacement's entrepreneurial epilogue

items: **Was Partition inevitable?** The historiography: League's determination + Congress's mistakes (1937 ministry-formation snub debate, mass-contact failure) + British grooves (electorates) + the 1946-47 violence spiral — best answer: **inevitable only in its last two years**; alternatives (Cabinet Mission federation) died of distrust, not design.

**Freedom-with-Partition's meaning**: sovereignty won by mass movement, yet the social fabric torn — Nehru's 'tryst' beside Gandhi's Calcutta fast is the era's honest portrait; the secular-state resolve (no two-nation logic conceded for those who remained) is Partition's constitutional rebuttal.

**Andhra register**: distant from the partition borders, Andhra's 1947-48 drama was **Hyderabad's accession** (next note) — but Partition touched the region via evacuee-property administration in Hyderabad state, and the secular-composite politics Andhra's leaders (Pattabhi as 1948 Congress president at Jaipur) carried into the republic's founding.

Numbers honestly banded: deaths 5-10+ lakh, displaced ~1.5 crore, women ~1 lakh — precision-claiming here reads as ignorance.

blocks.text: Exam tip: The two-image close — Nehru's Tryst at midnight, Gandhi fasting in Calcutta — earns the discursive mark; the rehabilitation paragraph (too often skipped) earns the content mark. Do both.

sections.heading: 🏺 Deep mastery — the road to 15 August & its price

items: **The final year:** the **Cabinet Mission (1946)** rejected Pakistan but proposed a loose federation; **Direct Action Day (Aug 1946)** and communal violence; the **Interim Government**; the **Mountbatten Plan (3 June 1947)**; and the **Radcliffe Line** partitioning Punjab & Bengal.
**The price:** the largest mass migration in history (~10-15 million displaced), communal carnage (~1 million dead), and the unresolved question of princely states and Kashmir.
**Why Partition:** the failure of power-sharing, League intransigence and Congress fatigue, colonial haste (advanced from June 1948 to August 1947), and the logic of the two-nation theory.
**Andhra register:** the region entered independence as part of Madras Presidency, its own statehood struggle (Visalandhra) still ahead.

prelimsPointers: **Radcliffe Line** — drew the India-Pakistan boundary (Punjab & Bengal).
**Mountbatten Plan (3 June 1947)** → **Indian Independence Act 1947** → power transfer 15 August 1947.
**Attlee's statement: 20 February 1947** (transfer by June 1948); **Mountbatten Plan: 3 June 1947**; **Indian Independence Act: 18 July 1947**.
**Radcliffe Boundary Commissions** (Punjab & Bengal); awards published **17 August 1947**.
Referendums: **NWFP & Sylhet (July 1947)**; Badshah Khan's Pathans boycotted NWFP's.
Gandhi spent 15 August 1947 in **Calcutta**; his Calcutta fast (Sept 1947) and last Delhi fast (**13-18 Jan 1948**); assassinated **30 January 1948**.
**Nilokheri township (S.K. Dey)** — 'Mazdoor Manzil' work-centred rehabilitation; **Kurukshetra camp** the largest.
**Abducted Persons (Recovery) Act 1949**; ~₹55 crore cash-balances dispute resolved after Gandhi's fast.
**Jaipur Congress 1948** presided by **Pattabhi Sitaramayya** — the Andhra man at the founding-era helm.
mainsAngles: Was Partition inevitable? Periodise the answer — long grooves, late inevitability.
Freedom arrived with a torn fabric — narrate the 1946-47 endgame from Direct Action to Radcliffe.
Rehabilitation was the republic's first governance test — assess the response from Kurukshetra to Nilokheri.
Why did Congress accept what it had always refused? Reconstruct the 1947 calculus.
The Constitution is Partition's rebuttal — discuss the secular-state resolve of the founding.

glossary.definition: The 3 June 1947 scheme — partition on communal-majority lines, dominion status at speed, princely states to choose — the endgame's blueprint.
The boundary drawn by Cyril Radcliffe's commissions through Punjab and Bengal — published after independence itself.
Assets left by migrants to the other dominion — administered/compensated under evacuee-property law; rehabilitation's currency.
The productivity-weighted unit used to allot East-Punjab land to refugees with graded cuts — planned rehabilitation's tool.
The Sept 1946 Congress-League executive under Nehru whose internal obstruction proved coalition impossible.
Nehru's midnight address of 14-15 August 1947 — the founding speech of the sovereign republic-to-be.

blocks.text: At lapse of paramountcy, **~565 princely states** (40% of area, ~24% of population) could join either dominion — in theory, none. **Patel + V.P. Menon** (States Department, July 1947) ran the playbook: **Instrument of Accession** (only defence-external affairs-communications) + **privy purses** + Mountbatten's persuasion → all but three signed by 15 August. The holdouts: **Junagadh** (Muslim ruler, Hindu majority → accession to Pakistan reversed by plebiscite, Feb 1948), **Kashmir** (standstill → tribal invasion Oct 1947 → accession 26 Oct 1947 → the enduring question), and **Hyderabad** — the Andhra syllabus's centre.

rows: The Nizam's gambit
Independence ambition (Osman Ali Khan); **Standstill Agreement (Nov 1947)**; arms procurement; **Razakars under Kasim Razvi (Ittehad-ul-Muslimeen)** terrorising the join-India movement
The people's struggle

**Hyderabad State Congress satyagraha (Swami Ramananda Tirtha)**; border camps from Indian territory; **Telangana's communist-led peasant struggle** simultaneously fighting Nizam-deshmukh order; Vande Mataram legacy cadres
**Operation Polo (Police Action), 13-17 September 1948**
Five days; Nizam surrendered; Razvi jailed; **communal violence in the aftermath — the Sundarlal Committee's report** (kept unpublished for decades) recorded large-scale killings: the honest asterisk
Aftermath

Military → civilian administration (M.K. Vellodi); Nizam as Rajpramukh; **mulki rules' continuation**; 1952 first elections; Hyderabad state lived until **1956's trifurcation** — Telangana to Andhra (→AP), Marathwada to Bombay, Kannada districts to Mysore

blocks.text: **Merger-to-reorganisation**: integration's second phase (mergers into unions/provinces, 1948-50) closed the map; then democracy asked the language question — **Potti Sriramulu's fast unto death (15 Oct–15 Dec 1952)** for a Telugu state from Madras → **Andhra State (1 Oct 1953, Kurnool capital)** — the **first linguistic state**, breaching the JVP Committee's (1949) caution → **Fazl Ali Commission/SRC (1953-55; States Reorganisation Act 1956)**: 14 states/6 UTs on language — **Andhra Pradesh (1 Nov 1956)** as Andhra + Telangana under the **Gentlemen's Agreement** (safeguards: regional council, mulki-type domicile rules, deputy-CM convention — their erosion seeds 2014's bifurcation: HCOA-068 completes this thread).

items: **Patel's method** = carrot (purses, honours), stick (Junagadh-Hyderabad demonstrations), and speed — 'the iron fist in the velvet glove'; Menon's drafting genius; Mountbatten's throne-to-throne persuasion: bloodless save the exceptions — a state-building feat with few parallels.

**Linguistic reorganisation's verdict**: feared as fissiparous, it proved **federal glue** — language-states deepened democracy (vernacular publics) without breaking unity; the counter-ledger: borders still contested (Belagavi), and the intra-state questions (Telangana within AP) that language alone couldn't settle.

**Andhra's double distinction**: the **first linguistic state (1953)** born of Sriramulu's sacrifice, and the **first SRC-era merger (1956)** whose safeguard-erosion became the first major un-merger (2014) — AP bookends India's states-reorganisation story.

items: The three-holdout structure + the Hyderabad table + the 1952-56 language chain is the complete architecture; the Sundarlal asterisk and Gentlemen's Agreement clauses are the honesty-and-depth markers.
Dates cold: 26 Oct 1947 (Kashmir), Feb 1948 (Junagadh plebiscite), 13-17 Sept 1948 (Polo), 15 Dec 1952 (Sriramulu), 1 Oct 1953, 1 Nov 1956.

blocks.text: Exam tip: For APPSC, the Hyderabad-Telangana strand is not a footnote but the headline — write Police Action WITH the people's struggle (Ramananda Tirtha + communist peasantry) and WITH the Sundarlal honesty, then carry the Gentlemen's Agreement forward to 2014.

sections.heading: 🏺 Deep mastery — integration of the princely states

items: **The task:** ~**565 princely states** to integrate; the **Instrument of Accession** (defence, external affairs, communications) engineered by **Sardar Patel & V.P. Menon** through the States Department.
**The hard cases:** **Junagadh** (plebiscite), **Hyderabad** (**Operation Polo, 1948** — police action against the Nizam/Razakars), and **Kashmir** (accession after the 1947 tribal invasion).
**Method:** a blend of persuasion, the appeal to patriotism, the 'privy purse' guarantee, and, where needed, force — 'the iron and velvet' of Patel's statecraft.
**AP link:** the **Hyderabad State** integration (1948) directly shaped the future Telangana region and, later, the Visalandhra question.

prelimsPointers: **Instrument of Accession** — Sardar Patel & V.P. Menon; ~565 princely states.
**Operation Polo (1948)** — integration of Hyderabad State (police action).
**Instrument of Accession**: defence, external affairs, communications; States Department (July 1947) — **Patel + V.P. Menon**.
**Junagadh**: plebiscite **Feb 1948**; **Kashmir accession: 26 October 1947** (Hari Singh; post-invasion).
**Operation Polo: 13-17 September 1948**; Hyderabad's militia — **Razakars (Kasim Razvi)**; **Sundarlal Committee** documented the aftermath.
**Hyderabad State Congress** leader: **Swami Ramananda Tirtha**; state's join-India satyagraha 1947-48.
**Potti Sriramulu** died **15 December 1952** (58-day fast, Madras) → **Andhra State 1 October 1953 (Kurnool capital; Prakasam first CM)**.
**JVP Committee (1949)**: Nehru-Patel-Pattabhi — cautious on linguistic states; **SRC/Fazl Ali (with K.M. Panikkar & H.N. Kunzru), report 1955; SR Act 1956** — 14 states, 6 UTs.
**Andhra Pradesh formed 1 November 1956** (first SRC-era merger) under the **Gentlemen's Agreement (Feb 1956)** — regional committee, domicile safeguards, deputy-CM convention.
Privy purses abolished by the **26th Amendment (1971)**.
mainsAngles: Integration of the states was the republic's first triumph — anatomise the Patel-Menon method and its three hard cases.
Hyderabad 1948 was accession, liberation and tragedy at once — write the layered account.
From Sriramulu's fast to the SRC — evaluate linguistic reorganisation as federal glue, not fissure.
The Gentlemen's Agreement was a merger's fine print — trace its safeguards and their erosion to 2014.
Compare Junagadh, Kashmir and Hyderabad as three grammars of accession.

glossary.definition: The Crown's suzerainty over princely states — lapsing at independence, leaving accession to rulers' choice.
The minimal treaty (three subjects) by which princely states joined a dominion — Menon's speed-friendly device.
Guaranteed payments to acceding rulers — integration's price, abolished in 1971.
Operation Polo (Sept 1948) — the five-day military integration of Hyderabad state.
Hyderabad-era domicile requirements for public employment — carried into AP's safeguards and the Telangana question.
The Andhra-Telangana pact of safeguards (regional committee, jobs, deputy-CM) conditioning the AP merger — its erosion fed bifurcation politics.

blocks.text: The **Constituent Assembly** (Cabinet-Mission framework; first met **9 December 1946**; sovereign after independence) worked 2 years 11 months 18 days through committees (Nehru — Union Powers & States; **Patel — Provincial, Minorities/FR (Advisory)**; Rajendra Prasad presiding; **Ambedkar's Drafting Committee**, with B.N. Rau's draft as base). Keystones: the **Objectives Resolution** (Dec 1946) becoming the Preamble; universal adult franchise at a stroke (democracy's largest wager); federalism with a strong centre (Partition's imprint); FRs + DPSPs (liberty and welfare braided); abolition of untouchability (Art 17); secular citizenship as the two-nation theory's rebuttal. **Andhra hands in the Assembly**: Pattabhi Sitaramayya, N.G. Ranga, **Durgabai Deshmukh** (one of the 15 women members), T. Prakasam, K. Santhanam-era Madras bench — the region present at the creation.

rows: Land reform (states)

**Zamindari abolition (Madras Estates Abolition Act 1948** covering Andhra estates; UP/Bihar acts 1950-51); tenancy reform; ceilings (patchy); the First Amendment (1951) + **Ninth Schedule** shielding reform from litigation
Planning
**Planning Commission (15 Mar 1950)**; **First Plan (1951-56)** — agriculture-Harrod-Domar; **Second Plan (1956-61)** — **Mahalanobis heavy-industry model**; steel trio (Bhilai-Rourkela-Durgapur)
Industrial framework
IPR **1948** (mixed economy) → IPR **1956** (the 'economic constitution': Schedule A public monopoly) + Industries Act 1951 (licensing)
Science-institutions

IITs (Kharagpur 1951–), CSIR labs, AEC (1948)/DAE (1954 — Bhabha), community development (**2 Oct 1952**) & NES; the dams — 'temples of modern India' (**Nagarjuna Sagar's foundation, 1955** — Nehru's phrase-site on Telugu soil; Bhakra, Hirakud, DVC)

items: **Non-alignment**: independence of judgment between blocs — not neutrality but 'enlightened self-interest' (keep both aid doors open, avoid entanglement); institutional arc — **Asian Relations Conference (Delhi 1947)** → **Bandung (1955**, Afro-Asian solidarity) → **NAM's Belgrade summit (1961**, Nehru-Tito-Nasser-Sukarno-Nkrumah).

**Panchsheel (29 April 1954**, China-Tibet trade agreement's preamble): five principles of coexistence — the idealist plank whose 1962 shattering (China war) is the standard critique; balanced verdict: NAM won India voice-beyond-weight and development space, but military unpreparedness (1962) exposed idealism's fiscal shadow.

**Neighbourhood & world**: Korea armistice diplomacy (Menon; NNRC chair 1953), Indus Waters Treaty (1960 — cooperation with Pakistan amid conflict), Goa's liberation (1961 — anti-colonial consistency over Western opinion), Commonwealth's republic formula (1949 — sovereignty inside association), UN peacekeeping tradition (Congo).

**The synthesis close**: the early republic's triad — **constitutional democracy + planned mixed economy + non-aligned autonomy** — one integrated founding project: political freedom institutionalised, economic freedom attempted, strategic freedom asserted; its incomplete legs (land reform's dilution, 1962, licence-raj's later costs) are the evaluation's honest counterweight.

items: Use the triad architecture (political-economic-strategic) for any 'early republic' question; each leg gets achievement + institution + critique.

Andhra anchors: Estates Abolition 1948, Nagarjuna Sagar 1955, Durgabai in the Assembly (and later Planning Commission/social welfare), first general election's Madras-state Andhra politics (Prakasam-era) — regional presence in every leg.

blocks.text: Exam tip: 'The Constitution answered Partition; the Plan answered poverty; non-alignment answered the Cold War' — that one-line triad, then the evidence, then the honest counterweights: the complete top-band shape.

sections.heading: 🏺 Deep mastery — nation-building: Constitution & foreign policy

items: **Constitution-making:** the Constituent Assembly (1946-49), the Objectives Resolution, and the founding of a democratic republic (link to Paper-III).

**Foreign policy — Nehru's grammar:** **Non-Alignment** (leadership of NAM, Bandung 1955), **Panchsheel (1954, with China)**, anti-colonialism, and the ideal of an independent voice — tested by the **1962 China war**.
**Early state-building:** linguistic reorganisation of states (**States Reorganisation Act 1956**), planning (Five-Year Plans, Mahalanobis), and the integration of a diverse polity.
**AP as the trigger:** **Andhra State (1953)**, born of Potti Sriramulu's sacrifice, forced the linguistic reorganisation of the whole country — a pivotal AP contribution to nation-building.

prelimsPointers: **Panchsheel (1954)** — Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence; **NAM** — Belgrade 1961 (roots at Bandung 1955).
**States Reorganisation Act 1956** — reorganised states on linguistic lines; **Andhra State 1953** was the first linguistic state.
mainsAngles: 'Andhra's creation in 1953 set in motion the linguistic reorganisation of India' — examine its national significance.

prelimsPointers: Constituent Assembly first met **9 Dec 1946**; Constitution adopted **26 Nov 1949**, in force **26 Jan 1950**; **15 women members** included **Durgabai Deshmukh**.
**First general election 1951-52** — ~17.3 crore electors, ~45% turnout: universal franchise's first test.
**Planning Commission: 15 March 1950**; **Second Plan (Mahalanobis, 1956)**; steel plants — **Bhilai (USSR), Rourkela (W. Germany), Durgapur (UK)**.
**IPR 1956** — 'economic constitution'; Industries (D&R) Act **1951** — licensing.
**Community Development Programme: 2 October 1952**; **Nagarjuna Sagar foundation: 1955** (Nehru; 'temples of modern India' idiom).
**Panchsheel: 29 April 1954** (India-China agreement on Tibet); **Bandung 1955**; **NAM Belgrade 1961**.
**Indus Waters Treaty 1960** (World Bank-brokered); **Goa liberated Dec 1961 (Operation Vijay)**.
**First Amendment (1951)** created the **Ninth Schedule** to shield land reform.
mainsAngles: The founding triad — Constitution, Plan, Non-alignment — was one project of freedom institutionalised: elaborate and evaluate.
Universal adult franchise was the founders' greatest wager — assess the first general election as democracy's proof.
From Estates Abolition to the Ninth Schedule — evaluate early land reform's promise and dilution with the Andhra evidence.
The Mahalanobis strategy built temples and queues alike — weigh the Second Plan's legacy.
Non-alignment was self-interest enlightened, not neutrality — assess Nehru's foreign policy through Bandung, Panchsheel and 1962.

glossary.definition: Nehru's December 1946 declaration of the Assembly's aims — sovereignty, justice, equality — transmuted into the Preamble.
The First Amendment's shelter for land-reform laws from fundamental-rights challenge — reform's constitutional armour.
The Second Plan's heavy-industry-first strategy — capital goods today for consumer goods tomorrow.
Independent judgment outside Cold-War blocs, preserving autonomy and aid access — India's founding strategic doctrine.
The five principles of peaceful coexistence (1954) — sovereignty, non-aggression, non-interference, equality, coexistence.
The 1952 block-based rural development apparatus — planning's village arm and Panchayati Raj's precursor.
